diagnostic_evidence.quote: The case $\eval = +\infty$ corresponds to the existence of $\evec \in \harmSpace$ such that $\bilIP{\evec}{\psi}{\osdomain_\ddindex} = 0$ for all $\psi \in \harmSpace$ but $\bilIP{\pu_\ddindex\evec}{\pu_\ddindex\widehat{\psi}}{\ovlpdomain_\ddindex} \neq 0$ for some $\widehat{\psi} \in \harmSpace$.

issues.failure_explanation: The restriction operator maps the a(D_i^*)-normed harmonic space into the a(\omega_i)-normed space, so its singular system must use \bilIP{\chi_i\varphi}{\chi_i\psi}{\omega_i} on the left and \bilIP{\varphi}{\psi}{D_i^*} on the right. The source integrates the left side over D_i^*, so the pencil is not the singular system of the stated restriction operator. The footnote's definition of the infinite-eigenvalue case itself uses the \omega_i form, confirming the intended domain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace D_i^* by \omega_i as the integration domain of the left bilinear form in eq:gevp and in eq:gevpSaddlePoint, and regenerate the local eigenproblems and numerical results based on the corrected saddle formulation.
issues.overall_effect: The local approximation estimate, exponential eigenvalue decay, global error estimate, divergence-free corollary, and MS-GFEM iteration theorem are all based on these eigenvalues. The mixed saddle formulation, which the paper states is used in the numerical simulations, contains the same wrong integration domain.
issues.title: Wrong integration domain in the local generalized eigenproblem
issues.why_classification: The mathematical correction is local and no theorem is abandoned, but the mixed formulation is the stated numerical algorithm, so a complete resolution requires changing the computed eigenproblems and rerunning the dependent numerical campaign. This is more than a typo-level repair, although no new proof architecture is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed constant divides by \norm{\velField}_{L^\infty}^2 and places \divergence \velField inside a radicand. The model assumptions allow \velField=0, giving a 0/0 expression, and they also allow \diffMin\,\divergence\velField/\norm{\velField}^2<-1 for nonzero velocity, giving the square root of a negative number. Thus the claimed explicit quantification of the constants does not cover admissible data.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the displayed formula to \velField\neq0 with nonnegative radicand, treat the pure-diffusion case as the corresponding limit, or replace the divergence term by an absolute-value bound and enlarge the constant.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constants in rm:constants cannot be used in the pure-diffusion case or in sufficiently strongly converging admissible velocity fields. The existence statement of th:msgfem:evaldecay is not itself invalidated by this remark-level formula.
issues.title: Explicit eigenvalue-decay constant is not defined for all admissible velocity fields
issues.why_classification: This is a contained parameter-regime repair in a remark; the main decay theorem and its downstream conclusions survive without major loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $C := \max_{\ddindex=1,\ldots,\nDoms} C_{\osdomain_\ddindex}$ with the Poincar\'{e} constants $C_{\osdomain_\ddindex}$ of $\osdomain_\ddindex$

Note that $\harmSpace$ equipped with $\bilIP{\cdot}{\cdot}{\osdomain_\ddindex}$ from \cref{eq:bilIP} is a Hilbert space unless $\osbdry \cap \bdryD = \emptyset$ and $\divergence \velField \equiv 0$ on $\osdomain_\ddindex$, in which case positive-definiteness is lost due to the existence of (non-zero) constant functions in $\harmSpace$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof uses a Poincaré constant on every oversampling subdomain. However, H^1_D(D_i^*) imposes zero only on \partial D_i^*\cap\Gamma_D; an interior oversampling domain may miss \Gamma_D entirely. In the divergence-free case assumed by the corollary, nonzero constants then lie in the local harmonic space. For a constant harmonic function w, \bilWF{w}{u} can be a nonzero boundary flux while \norm{w}_{a,D_i^*}=0, so the displayed relative continuity estimate is not justified for the harmonic-error space under the stated hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume that every oversampling subdomain meets \Gamma_D or otherwise satisfies the required Poincaré inequality, or replace the Poincaré-based step by a quotient/mean-zero Poincaré lemma for the local harmonic errors and adjust the continuity constant.
issues.overall_effect: The simplified divergence-free estimate loses its proof, and the choice of local dimensions in th:msgfem:iteration that relies on this corollary is affected. The general global theorem remains supported by the cited more general result.
issues.title: Missing Poincaré hypothesis in the divergence-free global-error corollary
issues.why_classification: The repair needs either a new hypothesis restricting the subdomain geometry or a contained new Poincaré-type argument for harmonic functions. A comparable divergence-free estimate survives, but the gap is not a one-line correction.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated error estimate is a global \Omega-norm estimate for the PDE solution. It does not imply the displayed local D_i^*-norm operator bound for every test function: a global norm can control the left-hand side on a subdomain, but it cannot replace \norm{\fwpTest}_{a,\Omega} by \norm{\fwpTest}_{a,D_i^*}. The needed uniform contraction estimate is therefore unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the global error estimate to an arbitrary function w and prove \norm{(I-\msgfemOperator)w}_{a,\Omega}\leq\vartheta\norm{w}_{a,\Omega}; use this global contraction in the iteration recurrence.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the contraction and strict monotone convergence of the MS-GFEM iteration fails. The theorem statement itself is not shown to be false; only the argument contains an unjustified norm inference.
issues.title: Global MS-GFEM error estimate is used to claim a local operator contraction
issues.why_classification: Replacing the unsupported local norm estimate by the corresponding global estimate is a short repair that preserves the stated convergence theorem and its conclusion.
